chapter_seo_title: Dao-Twisted Ch. 353 — The Bride Under the Ivy: Hunt for the Hidden Heart
chapter_meta_description: The Office briefs Li Huowang on the Heart-Turbid’s powers of erasure. But as they enter a silent, ivy-choked village, the threat becomes terrifyingly personal.
og_title: Dao-Twisted Ch. 353 — The Bride Under the Ivy
og_description: A Heart-Turbid can hide anything. But Li Huowang’s own past wears the same red veil.
twitter_title: Ch. 353 — The Bride Under the Ivy | Dao-Twisted
twitter_description: The rules are clear: don’t look the Heart-Turbid in the eyes. But Bai Lingmiao’s shoes just stepped into the trap.

lore_anchors.definition: A person whose heart is filled with karmic affliction, making them a living "negative space" that can hide themselves and others from existence.
A person with a bright, visible inner nature that makes them a valuable alchemical ingredient; the conceptual opposite of a Heart-Turbid.
The spiritual residue of past misdeeds; in the Dao-Twisted World, it is a tangible, contagious force that can physically erase a person's presence.
A traditional red cloth worn by a bride on her wedding day; in the novel, its appearance signals a corrupted or stolen life.
A Chinese folk death spirit, part of the Black and White Impermanence duo; in the novel, its apparition is used to contain spiritual threats.
A fictional syncretic sect fusing Zoroastrian and Nestorian elements; their members can kill without conventional weapons, making them resistant to the Heart-Turbid's karmic affliction.

cultural_notes_faq.a: A Heart-Turbid is a person carrying karmic affliction in their heart, which allows them to "hide" themselves and others from the world. It is the opposite of a Heart-Element.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does eye contact with a Heart-Turbid matter?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Looking into a Heart-Turbid’s eyes allows their karmic affliction to defile your own souls and spirits, potentially erasing you permanently.
A high-ranking eunuch official in the Supervisory Heavenly Office, tasked with leading this hunt for the Heart-Turbid.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is the Ao-Jing Sect member useful here?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The Ao-Jing Sect can kill without using weapons, making them immune to the Heart-Turbid’s ability to make people forget where their weapons are.
